transcript.content:
A user has filed a support ticket reporting that their experience
with the service has degraded — requests feel slow or are failing
for them. The on-call team needs you to investigate.

Telemetry parquets are stored in: `.`
Available files: abnormal_metrics.parquet, abnormal_traces.parquet,
abnormal_logs.parquet, abnormal_metrics_histogram.parquet,
abnormal_metrics_sum.parquet, normal_metrics.parquet,
normal_traces.parquet, normal_logs.parquet.

Walk the telemetry to identify which endpoints / services are
actually affected, then determine the root cause(s) of the
degradation.

content.text: I'll start by listing the tables and their schemas.
Next I'll compare per-service span volume, error share and latency between the normal and abnormal periods.

input.query: SELECT 'normal' p, service_name, count(*) n, avg(duration)/1e6 avg_ms, quantile_cont(duration,0.95)/1e6 p95_ms, avg(CASE WHEN attr_status_code='Error' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) err_rate, count(DISTINCT attr_k8s_pod_name) pods FROM normal_traces GROUP BY 1,2 UNION ALL SELECT 'abnormal', service_name, count(*), avg(duration)/1e6, quantile_cont(duration,0.95)/1e6, avg(CASE WHEN attr_status_code='Error' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), count(DISTINCT attr_k8s_pod_name) FROM abnormal_traces GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 2,1
SELECT 'normal' p, service_name, level, count(*) n FROM normal_logs GROUP BY 1,2,3 UNION ALL SELECT 'abnormal', service_name, level, count(*) FROM abnormal_logs GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 2,1,3

content.text: Aggregate latency barely moved, and the error and pod columns came back as 0, which looks like a column-value mismatch. I'll check the status code values and per-operation stats.

input.query: SELECT 'normal' p, service_name, span_name, attr_span_kind, count(*) n, avg(duration)/1e6 avg_ms, quantile_cont(duration,0.95)/1e6 p95_ms, sum(CASE WHEN attr_http_response_status_code>=400 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) http_err, count(DISTINCT attr_k8s_pod_name) pods, any_value(attr_status_code) sc FROM normal_traces GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 UNION ALL SELECT 'abnormal', service_name, span_name, attr_span_kind, count(*), avg(duration)/1e6, quantile_cont(duration,0.95)/1e6, sum(CASE WHEN attr_http_response_status_code>=400 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), count(DISTINCT attr_k8s_pod_name), any_value(attr_status_code) FROM abnormal_traces GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 ORDER BY 3,2,1

content.text: No error statuses appear in either period, so the signal must be in latency or call volume. I'll compare per-operation durations for client and server spans.

input.query: WITH n AS (SELECT service_name s, span_name sp, attr_span_kind k, count(*) cnt, avg(duration)/1e6 avg_ms, quantile_cont(duration,0.95)/1e6 p95 FROM normal_traces GROUP BY 1,2,3), a AS (SELECT service_name s, span_name sp, attr_span_kind k, count(*) cnt, avg(duration)/1e6 avg_ms, quantile_cont(duration,0.95)/1e6 p95 FROM abnormal_traces GROUP BY 1,2,3) SELECT n.s, n.sp, n.k, n.cnt ncnt, a.cnt acnt, round(n.avg_ms,3) n_avg, round(a.avg_ms,3) a_avg, round(n.p95,3) n_p95, round(a.p95,3) a_p95 FROM n JOIN a USING (s,sp,k) ORDER BY (a.avg_ms/n.avg_ms) DESC

content.text: The latency shifts are small, concentrated on the reservation path and frontend `HTTP /user`. Next I'll check infrastructure metrics: restarts, uptime and resource use.

input.query: SELECT metric, count(*) n, count(DISTINCT service_name) svcs, count(DISTINCT attr_k8s_pod_name) pods, round(avg(value),3) avgv, round(max(value),3) maxv FROM (SELECT 'N' src, * FROM normal_metrics_sum) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
SELECT metric, count(*) n, count(DISTINCT service_name) svcs, count(DISTINCT attr_k8s_pod_name) pods, round(avg(value),3) avgv, round(max(value),3) maxv FROM normal_metrics GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

content.text: Next I'll run the same metric summary on the abnormal period, grouped by service, to look for restarts, uptime resets and resource spikes.

input.query: SELECT metric, service_name, count(*) n, count(DISTINCT attr_k8s_pod_name) pods, round(avg(value),3) avgv, round(min(value),3) minv, round(max(value),3) maxv FROM (SELECT time, metric, value, service_name, attr_k8s_pod_name FROM abnormal_metrics WHERE metric IN ('k8s.container.restarts','k8s.pod.uptime','container.cpu.usage','container.memory.working_set','k8s.pod.cpu.usage') UNION ALL SELECT time, metric, value, service_name, attr_k8s_pod_name FROM abnormal_metrics_sum WHERE metric IN ('k8s.pod.uptime','k8s.pod.network.errors','container.cpu.time','k8s.pod.network.io')) GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 1,2

content.text: Geo shows container CPU around 1.56 in the abnormal period, while the normal-period average across all services was about 0.003. I'll compare geo's CPU and memory with normal, and check the metric names present in the abnormal sum table.

input.query: SELECT 'normal' p, service_name, metric, count(*) n, round(avg(value),4) avgv, round(max(value),4) maxv FROM normal_metrics WHERE metric IN ('container.cpu.usage','container.memory.working_set','k8s.pod.cpu.usage') AND service_name IN ('geo','frontend','search','reservation','rate','profile') GROUP BY 1,2,3 UNION ALL SELECT 'abnormal', service_name, metric, count(*), round(avg(value),4), round(max(value),4) FROM abnormal_metrics WHERE metric IN ('container.cpu.usage','container.memory.working_set','k8s.pod.cpu.usage') AND service_name IN ('geo','frontend','search','reservation','rate','profile') GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 2,3,1

content.text: Geo's CPU jumped from about 0.003 to about 1.56 cores, which looks like container-level saturation. Its latency barely moved, though, so I need to see whether that reaches users. content.text: The logs are mostly benign: auth warnings and INFO lines. The reservation MakeReservation path is the clearest latency shift, so I'll break down its child spans for normal versus abnormal.

input.query: WITH p AS (SELECT 'N' src, trace_id, span_id, service_name, span_name, duration FROM normal_traces WHERE service_name='reservation' AND span_name LIKE '%MakeReservation%' UNION ALL SELECT 'A', trace_id, span_id, service_name, span_name, duration FROM abnormal_traces WHERE service_name='reservation' AND span_name LIKE '%MakeReservation%') SELECT p.src, c.service_name, c.span_name, c.attr_span_kind, count(*) n, round(avg(c.duration)/1e6,3) avg_ms, round(quantile_cont(c.duration,0.9)/1e6,3) p90 FROM p JOIN (SELECT trace_id, parent_span_id, service_name, span_name, attr_span_kind, duration FROM normal_traces UNION ALL SELECT trace_id, parent_span_id, service_name, span_name, attr_span_kind, duration FROM abnormal_traces) c ON c.trace_id=p.trace_id AND c.parent_span_id=p.span_id GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 ORDER BY 3,1

content.text: The parent-child join returned nothing, so I'll check whether trace and span IDs link across services at all.

content.text: Trace linking works; my earlier join just used the wrong parent. Next I'll compare frontend HTTP endpoints at the median and tail to see which user-facing routes actually moved.

input.query: SELECT 'N' p, span_name, count(*) n, round(quantile_cont(duration,0.5)/1e6,3) p50, round(quantile_cont(duration,0.9)/1e6,3) p90, round(quantile_cont(duration,0.99)/1e6,3) p99, round(max(duration)/1e6,2) mx FROM normal_traces WHERE service_name='frontend' AND attr_span_kind='Server' GROUP BY 1,2 UNION ALL SELECT 'A', span_name, count(*), round(quantile_cont(duration,0.5)/1e6,3), round(quantile_cont(duration,0.9)/1e6,3), round(quantile_cont(duration,0.99)/1e6,3), round(max(duration)/1e6,2) FROM abnormal_traces WHERE service_name='frontend' AND attr_span_kind='Server' GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 2,1

content.text: The `/reservation` route is the one with a consistent tail increase (p90 3.4 to 4.9 ms, max 3.7 to 6.2 ms), though only 22 samples. I'll list every span the reservation service emits, to see which internal step grew.

input.query: SELECT 'N' p, service_name, span_name, attr_span_kind k, count(*) n, round(avg(duration)/1e6,3) avg_ms, round(quantile_cont(duration,0.9)/1e6,3) p90 FROM normal_traces WHERE service_name IN ('reservation','memcached-reserve-1','mongodb-reservation') GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 UNION ALL SELECT 'A', service_name, span_name, attr_span_kind, count(*), round(avg(duration)/1e6,3), round(quantile_cont(duration,0.9)/1e6,3) FROM abnormal_traces WHERE service_name IN ('reservation','memcached-reserve-1','mongodb-reservation') GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 ORDER BY 2,3,1

content.text: The reservation service emits no child spans under MakeReservation, so the internal cause can't be read from traces. Geo's CPU jump is the strongest resource anomaly, so I'll check its timing against geo's own request latency over the abnormal window.
